subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Valence shell
hotspots.description: The outer ring is the valence shell — the outermost layer of the atom. The electrons living on it are the valence electrons.
hotspots.positionHint: The outermost ring of the sodium atom, larger and brighter than the inner ring.
hotspots.function: Marks the outermost shell that holds the valence electrons.

hotspots.label: Valence electron
hotspots.description: This single electron on the outer ring is sodium's valence electron. It is the one that gets given away when sodium bonds with chlorine.
hotspots.positionHint: The single larger electron dot sitting on the outer ring.
hotspots.function: Shows the outer-shell electron that does the bonding.

hotspots.label: Inner electrons
hotspots.description: The smaller electron dots on the inner ring are inner electrons. They stay buried in the atom and are not involved in bonding.
hotspots.positionHint: The smaller, dimmer electron dots on the inner ring.
hotspots.function: Shows the inner electrons that do not bond.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A sodium atom floats centered, large in frame, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Sodium is a soft muted violet sphere with two translucent hairline shell rings; inner electrons are small dim dots, the valence electron is larger and brighter. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the valence electron (molecular-green / amber / slate accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Sodium sphere: soft muted violet matte, roughness ~0.5. Shell rings: thin translucent hairline circles (alpha ~0.2). Inner electrons: small dim teal dots, roughness ~0.5. Valence electron: slightly larger, brighter teal dot with a subtle spec, roughness ~0.4. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a sodium atom showing its valence electron, built to be read as 'the outermost electron is the one that bonds.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a ball model of a sodium atom — soft muted violet nucleus sphere (radius ~0.5), two translucent hairline shell rings at radii ~0.85 and ~1.35. Inner ring carries EIGHT small dim teal electron dots (radius ~0.05); outer ring carries ONE larger brighter teal electron dot (radius ~0.09) at the top.

2) BONDING TRANSFER (toggleable layer): a soft muted green chlorine atom (radius ~0.45) appears to the right, its shell ring with SEVEN dots and one empty spot. The sodium valence electron animates along a curved dashed path over to chlorine's empty spot (app-driven), and a + appears over sodium / − over chlorine (app-drawn UI glyphs).

3) SHELL COUNT (toggleable layer): inner electrons dim to near-invisible while the valence electron stays bright, emphasizing that only the outer one matters for bonding.

Camera: framed so the sodium atom is large and centered; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: SodiumNucleus, ShellRing_Inner, ShellRing_Outer, InnerElectrons_08, ValenceElectron_01, ChlorineAtom, ChlorineShell, ChlorineElectrons_07, TransferPath, TransferDot. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
